field_checks.summary: Readability was verified for the requested source, packet, work, final, worker-log, and report paths. Independent XML/supplement parsing matched final activity coverage: 12 PA-Win2 Table 2 MIC/MBC rows plus 4 Supplement Table S1 P. aeruginosa ATCC 9027 condition rows; toxicity has 3 source-supported cell-viability rows.

The database layer correctly keeps all 13 DBAASP fallback rows as unresolved_record with source_verified=0 and authoritative_dbaasp_ingest_ready=false, but final database records still contain 117 malformed candidate locator fields with double prefixes such as xml:xml:* and pdf:pdf:* under record_audits[].source_review candidate locator arrays.

Every current paper-final JSON record was reviewed. Paper and packet final mirrors are byte-identical for common files; packet-only mechanism_evidence.json is a byte-identical declared alias of mechanism_ontology_record.json. Review counts match live final arrays, and review_report open_rework_ticket_count=0 matches analysis_status and computed live ticket state.

Mechanism ontology preserves evidence-strength boundaries: 6 claims total; only the DiSC3(5) membrane depolarization assay is direct_mechanism, while time-kill and biofilm are phenotype_supported, RT-qPCR claims are inferred_mechanism, and in-silico discovery/modeling is computational_only.

Primary paper identity and entity sequence are source-supported: DOI 10.3390/antibiotics13121113, PMCID PMC11672609, PMID 39766503, PA-Win2 sequence LLRGLRYLCLKILYILKLRK from the Table 1 20-mer candidate, with no final objects containing both sequence and sequence_length. However, database candidate identity linkage is not publication-grade because redundant candidate locator fields in final database records are malformed and non-resolving.

Activity/toxicity units and normalization statuses are source-reviewable and direct or censored as appropriate, and strict source_locator fields do not contain project artifact paths. The database final still fails locator normalization because record_audits[].source_review.candidate_name_locator_ids and candidate_sequence_locator_ids include xml:xml:* and pdf:pdf:* values that do not resolve to packet locators.

No project artifact path was found in strict source_locator/source_locators/locator fields, and fallback release boundary is preserved: linked authoritative database rows are absent, all 13 fallback rows remain unresolved_record, and authoritative_dbaasp_ingest_ready is false. The malformed double-prefix source locators are a locator-normalization blocker, not a recursive-authority promotion.

Current review preserves two database cautions: no linked authoritative APD6/DBAASP/DRAMP rows are present, and DBAASP machine fallback rows remain unresolved candidate provenance. No source_conflict can be adjudicated from authoritative rows because linked authoritative snapshots are empty.

All staged supplementary material was inspected: the staged ZIP contains one PDF member, extracted to packet supplementary surfaces; supplementary_text has 9 page records, supplementary_tables has S1/S2/S3 with 4/34/14 rows, archive manifest records extraction, and extraction_errors.jsonl is empty.

Final toxicity/selectivity coverage matches the primary source: HaCaT has no observed viability decrease through the highest tested concentration, while hADMSC and HDFalpha decrease above 64 ug/mL. Toxicity rows preserve target_class, cell_line, target species, units, censored status, and source locators.

blocking_findings.reason: The current paper and packet final database_record_verification.json records contain 117 non-resolving candidate locator values under record_audits[0..12].source_review.candidate_name_locator_ids and candidate_sequence_locator_ids. Examples include xml:xml:article-title:1, xml:xml:abstract:1, xml:xml:p:3, xml:xml:sec:4, xml:xml:sec:5, xml:xml:table-wrap:1, and pdf:pdf:page=3, while the source surfaces resolve at xml:article-title:1, xml:abstract:1, xml:p:3, xml:sec:4, xml:sec:5, xml:table-wrap:1, and pdf:page=3. Because those objects also assert candidate_name_locator_match=true and candidate_sequence_locator_match=true, the database identity artifact is not field-level source-reviewable even though the fallback rows remain correctly unresolved and excluded from authoritative ingest.
required_actions: Normalize or remove the redundant malformed candidate_name_locator_ids and candidate_sequence_locator_ids in the worker-4 database artifact and both final mirrors; use canonical packet locators, not double-prefixed strings.
Preserve all 13 DBAASP fallback candidate rows as unresolved_record and keep authoritative_dbaasp_ingest_ready=false unless linked authoritative rows are added and source-reviewed.
Re-run a resolver check against locator_index.json, xml_sections.json, and pdf_text.jsonl over record_audits[].source_review candidate locator arrays after repair.
acceptance_checks: A recursive Python check over both final database mirrors reports malformed_candidate_locator_count == 0 for prefixes xml:xml:, pdf:pdf:, and supp:supp:.

Every locator under record_audits[].source_review.candidate_name_locator_ids and candidate_sequence_locator_ids resolves to locator_index.json, xml_sections.json, pdf_text.jsonl, or a declared database locator.
database_record_verification.json status_summary remains source_verified=0 and unresolved_record=13, and authoritative_dbaasp_ingest_ready remains false.
Paper-final and packet-final database_record_verification.json remain byte-identical after the repair.

cautions.summary: No linked authoritative APD6/DBAASP/DRAMP article, assay, sequence, or literature rows are present. Paper-level source review may be retained as pilot evidence, but authoritative DBAASP ingest is not ready.

All 13 DBAASP machine fallback rows are preserved as unresolved_record candidate provenance and excluded from authoritative/RC2/portal ingest; this boundary is correct but remains a release limitation.
